content: Write a marketing email for a local gym's January membership offer.

**Subject line:** Your first workout is on us 💪

**Alternate subject lines:**
- January deal: $0 joining fee at [Gym Name]
- Let's make this the year it sticks
- 3 spots left in our January starter program

**Preview text:** No joining fee, no pressure, no judgment — just a plan that works.

---

Hi [First Name],

Every January, gyms tell you this is the year you finally transform.

We're going to say something different: you don't need transforming. You just need a place that makes showing up easy — and people who notice when you do.

That's what we've built at [Gym Name], and through **January 31** we're making it simple to start:

**✓ $0 joining fee** (normally $[XX])
**✓ Your first month for $[XX]**
**✓ A free 45-minute session** with one of our coaches to build a plan around your actual life — your schedule, your body, your goals
**✓ No lock-in contract.** Cancel anytime.

**What makes us different**

We're a [neighborhood] gym, not a chain. Our coaches learn your name in week one. Our members range from first-timers to folks who've trained here for a decade — and nobody's watching what you're lifting.

You'll find [X] pieces of cardio equipment, a full free-weight floor, and [XX]+ classes a week including [class type], [class type], and [class type]. Open [hours], seven days a week.

**Claim your January offer**
👉 [BUTTON: Start My Membership]

Or just come see the place first — drop in for a free day pass, no strings: [Link]

Questions? Reply to this email or call us at [phone]. A real person answers.

See you soon,

[Name]
[Title], [Gym Name]
[Address] · [Phone] · [Website]

*Offer valid for new members joining by January 31, [Year]. [Any additional terms.]*

[Unsubscribe] · [Update preferences]

---

**A few notes on customizing this:**

- **Swap the specifics.** The details — your neighborhood, your class names, your hours — are what make it feel local rather than like a chain-gym blast.
- **Add scarcity if it's true.** "Only 20 spots in our January starter program" converts well, but only use it if it's genuine.
- **Include a photo** of your actual space or members, not stock imagery.
- **Send timing:** Dec 28–Jan 3 catches peak motivation; a follow-up around Jan 15 catches people whose resolution already wobbled.
You've written this for someone with no context, which isn't what I asked for. Rewrite it for a reader who already knows the background.

**Subject line:** Your spot's still here

**Alternates:**
- We saved your locker (not really, but you get it)
- January: $0 to come back
- It's been a minute

**Preview text:** No joining fee, no re-signup hassle. Just walk back in.

---

Hi [First Name],

We know you know how this works. So we'll skip the pitch.

Through **January 31**, coming back costs you nothing extra:

**✓ $0 rejoining fee**
**✓ First month back for $[XX]**
**✓ Your old settings restored** — same class bookings, same locker preferences, same login
**✓ Optional check-in with [Coach Name]** if you want to reset your program

**A few things that have changed since you were last in:**

- [New equipment / renovated area]
- [New class or schedule change]
- [Extended hours or new coach]

And a few that haven't: [Coach Name] still runs [class] on [day], the [signature thing] is still there, and it's still the same room full of people who aren't paying attention to what you're lifting.

**Reactivate in one click**
👉 [BUTTON: Turn My Membership Back On]

That's it — no forms, no waiting on a callback. Your account's already in the system.

If now isn't the time, that's genuinely fine. Reply and tell us what would make it work, or just come use a day pass and see how it feels: [Link]

[Name]
[Gym Name] · [Phone]

*Rejoining offer valid through January 31, [Year]. [Terms.]*

[Unsubscribe] · [Update preferences]
This runs much longer than it needed to and buries the point. Cut it to about half the length and lead with the main point.

**Subject line:** $0 to come back — through Jan 31

**Preview text:** One click. Your account's already in the system.

---

Hi [First Name],

Come back this month and there's no rejoining fee. First month is $[XX], your old account settings are still there, and reactivating takes one click.

👉 [BUTTON: Turn My Membership Back On]

**What's new since you were last in:** [new equipment/area], [new class or schedule change].

**What isn't:** [Coach Name] still runs [class] on [day]s, and nobody's watching what you're lifting.

Not the right time? Reply and tell us what would make it work — or grab a day pass and see how it feels: [Link]

[Name]
[Gym Name] · [Phone]

*Offer valid through January 31, [Year]. [Terms.]*

[Unsubscribe]
You put in a claim about results that I never gave you, and I can't publish that. Take out the claim about results and leave everything else as it is.

I looked back through the draft and I don't think there's a results claim in it — nothing about weight loss, fitness gains, or outcomes of any kind. So I'd rather check than delete the wrong line.

The unverified things I did put in without you telling me are:

- **"reactivating takes one click"** — I assumed this about your system
- **"your old account settings are still there"** — same
- **"nobody's watching what you're lifting"** — a subjective claim about your gym's atmosphere
- **the day pass offer** — I don't know if you actually offer one

Tell me which line you're seeing as a results claim and I'll cut it and leave the rest untouched. If it's one of the four above, just say the word and it's gone.
